Subject: ACME POC — post-demo recap & next steps

Thanks again for your time today — great discussion. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

Summary / objectives
- Goal: validate Redwood inference for ACME’s customer support summarization use case (reduce agent handle time; prioritize high precision on important fields).
- Success criteria (draft): 
  - Extraction accuracy (entity F1) >= 0.86 on ACME holdout dataset
  - Latency: 95th percentile < 600ms for 512-token context
  - Hallucination rate (false positive critical fields) < 2%
  - Business score (weighted): accuracy 60%, latency 25%, reliability 15%

Proposed POC / timeline
- Redwood provides a 2-week trial environment + evaluation harness.
- Proposed start: week of 2027-04-04; flexible if you need more lead time.
- Deliverables: evaluation plan (attached), success criteria (attached), integration checklist.

Owners / asks
- ACME technical lead: Tom Brooks — owns data access, test accounts, and network whitelisting.
- ACME product lead: Samantha Green — owns business success signoff.
- Redwood engineering lead: Dylan Brooks — owns integration and runtime config.
- Action items for ACME: confirm start date, share sample dataset (anonymized) + expected QPS and peak concurrency, and confirm who will approve success at the end of the trial.

Attachments: acme-poc-success-criteria.xlsx, acme-eval-plan-v1.md

Happy to jump on a quick call if helpful.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Subject: RE: ACME POC — post-demo recap & next steps

Appreciate the quick replies — shifting the start to week of 2027-04-11 is fine. Updated plan attached (acme-eval-plan-v1.md). High-level eval methodology proposal — please review and flag anything missing: 

Evaluation approach (short)
- Offline eval: run Redwood against ACME holdout dataset (sanitized) using the evaluation harness. Metrics produced: entity F1, precision/recall per entity, hallucination rate (false positives), and latency percentiles. This is the deterministic baseline.
- Online shadowing: deploy model in shadow mode for 3 full business days (no agent-facing output) to capture distribution shift and end-to-end latency under real traffic.
- Acceptance criteria: offline F1 >= threshold (TBD after we see sample), no regression in latency beyond SLO, and shadow pass showing comparable distribution to offline. Final business signoff from Samantha.

Grading rubric (recommended)
- Entity F1 (weighted 60%): baseline target 0.86; scoring bands for 0.80-0.86 (partial credit), >0.86 (full).
- Latency (weighted 25%): 95p < 600ms = full credit; 600–800ms = partial; >800ms = fail unless compensated by strong accuracy.
- Hallucination / false positive rate (weighted 15%): <2% = full; 2–5% = partial; >5% = fail.

Ownership
- Redwood runtime/integration: Dylan Brooks (dylan.brooks@redwood.ai)
- Offline eval harness / grading: Rachel Kim (rachel.kim@redwood.ai)
- ACME data & access: Tom Brooks
- Business decision: Samantha Green

Attachments: acme-eval-plan-v1.md

Next steps
1) ACME: confirm start week (you indicated 2027-04-11) + share sample dataset by 2027-03-30.
2) Redwood: prepare eval harness and baseline run; Rachel will run initial offline tests as soon as dataset is available.

If that looks good I'll update the plan with exact scoring bands after reviewing the sample.

Thanks,
Marissa
